clm-f36d1a0b6c73fdf47279.text: Agarwal explains Shapley values with a gloves example: with one seller of a left glove and two sellers of a right glove, the Shapley math pays about 4x more for the scarce left glove.

clm-3ba8477483de4dcadd8f.text: Agarwal says that three years ago he became convinced agents will use the web 1000x more than humans ever have.

clm-86a9b1378b74a6c9cb3d.text: Agarwal argues the web runs on three business models, subscriptions, advertising, and transactions, and the first two depend on human attention, which agents do not supply, so a new model is needed.

clm-c5f66ebcb55b87d91ec4.text: Agarwal says content that gives agents a recipe, a plan for how to tackle a kind of problem, is also cited and rewarded, not just raw facts.

clm-03cf344f410a7b42f764.text: The licenses SpaceX acquired from Grain Management are in the 800-megahertz band, tailored for wireless service from cellphone towers rather than satellites.

evidence.locator: § SpaceX Buys More Spectrum: “The U.S. licenses, which are in the 800-megahertz band, are tailored for wireless service from cellphone towers rather than satellites.”

clm-2faad048137f0f8aeff6.text: Following news of SpaceX's spectrum purchase, shares in AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile each fell more than 6% in post-close trading, while SpaceX shares gained roughly 3% to $165.10 after hours.

evidence.locator: § SpaceX Buys More Spectrum: “Shares in AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile all fell more than 6% in post-close trading.”

clm-a79f59e1f2d38dab261f.text: In September 2025 SpaceX acquired H-Block and AWS-4 spectrum from EchoStar, which faced coverage hurdles because AWS-4 was not approved for satellite-to-handset communication and EchoStar had configured uplink bands for downlink.

evidence.locator: § SpaceX Buys More Spectrum: “SpaceX acquired H-Block and AWS-4 spectrum from EchoStar”

clm-16b9f357b6f2a89c16ad.text: Rather than partnering with Starlink, AT&T and Verizon doubled down on AST SpaceMobile for satellite connectivity, while Apple allied with Amazon through its Globalstar purchase.

evidence.locator: § SpaceX Buys More Spectrum: “AT&T and Verizon doubled down on AST SpaceMobile”

clm-ef44a14e0660782fa397.text: Thompson argues major telecommunications carriers and tech companies avoided partnering with Starlink because none wanted to become beholden to Elon Musk.

evidence.locator: § SpaceX Buys More Spectrum: “none of the companies wanted to be beholden to Elon Musk.”

clm-5a5a5236fee6dcffd8fb.text: In November 2025 SpaceX bought the AWS-3 spectrum block from EchoStar to secure expansive uplink capacity matching its AWS-4 purchase, awaiting satellite-to-handset regulatory approval.

evidence.locator: § Musk and Market Structure: “the company bought the AWS-3 spectrum block from EchoStar that provided much more expansive uplink capacity”

clm-6225bc579eecd105c82a.text: Delta Air Lines CEO Ed Bastian stated that Delta tested Starlink in-flight internet but chose not to partner with it due to personal reluctance to work with Elon Musk.

evidence.locator: § Musk and Market Structure: “Ed also said that DL did test with starlink, but did not want to partner with Elon.”

clm-889762c9db7130b2fa35.text: United Airlines had completed 41% of its Starlink in-flight internet installation rollout across its fleet as of October 2026.

evidence.locator: § Musk and Market Structure: “United rollout is only 41% complete.”

clm-ca2af16c592865cbddef.text: Southwest Airlines began installing Starlink satellite internet on its aircraft as part of its passenger experience upgrades.

evidence.locator: § Musk and Market Structure: “Southwest has started its Starlink installation”

clm-09a0a8d61c97ac5313bc.text: American Airlines expanded its Starlink satellite internet commitment to cover its entire mainline jet fleet.

evidence.locator: § Musk and Market Structure: “American Airlines has upped its Starlink commitment”

clm-f4dbbd0618cc864fe610.text: Thompson argues Delta risks undermining its premium airline positioning by enduring inferior connectivity while awaiting Amazon Leo as competitors deploy fast Starlink WiFi.

evidence.locator: § Musk and Market Structure: “Delta has to endure the messy middle where some flights are awesome and some aren’t.”

clm-c39aca871ca937bdba11.text: Thompson argues Elon Musk approaches industries by seeking to reshape market structure so that his companies' victory becomes inevitable regardless of customer or rival personal sentiment.

evidence.locator: § Musk and Market Structure: “his goal is to fundamentally reshape the market structure such that his companies’ victory is inevitable”

clm-0d1100ec9d35fb841e67.text: SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell stated that SpaceX intends to build out a terrestrial mobile component by mounting cellular base stations directly onto the gear holding Starlink broadband dishes.

evidence.locator: § Distributed Cellular: “you could put a base station, a cellular base station on the — basically the gear that holds a Starlink broadband dish.”

clm-0d1100ec9d35fb841e67.notes: Conflict with clm-203e7cb2348547cb6706: Shotwell explains SpaceX can mount small base stations on dishes rather than building traditional cell towers.

clm-72aa97b9f9f622f569a9.text: Shotwell stated that deploying femtocell base stations on customer Starlink dish mounts allows SpaceX to expand terrestrial mobile coverage as needed without spending billions upfront on low-band spectrum.

evidence.locator: § Distributed Cellular: “You don’t have to necessarily spend many billions of dollars in low-band spectrum all upfront before you deploy your system.”

clm-71461a9375419d0cec84.text: Elon Musk stated SpaceX plans to deploy small cellular base stations on rooftop Starlink antennas across homes and businesses, avoiding the expensive buildout of large cell towers.

evidence.locator: § Distributed Cellular: “Instead of having to deploy these very expensive and difficult-to-locate large cellular base stations, we feel reasonably confident that we can deploy a large number of sort of small stations.”

clm-71461a9375419d0cec84.notes: Conflict with clm-203e7cb2348547cb6706: Musk explains SpaceX avoids large cell towers by deploying small stations on rooftop Starlink antennas.

clm-ec75e662d96d2296663b.text: Thompson argues Starlink's satellite constellation gives its network ubiquitous backhaul everywhere, enabling a mesh network of small-scale rooftop access points rather than costly fiber-linked towers.

evidence.locator: § Distributed Cellular: “Thanks to the company’s satellite constellation its future network basically has backhaul everywhere; the way to leverage that is not with ultra-powerful nodes but rather what is basically a mesh network of smaller scale access points.”

clm-4a697ca4cf41027ad1eb.text: SpaceX's purchased 800-megahertz spectrum licenses were previously utilized for Sprint's old Nextel push-to-talk network, providing low frequencies that penetrate building walls.

evidence.locator: § Distributed Cellular: “This latest spectrum purchase was previously used for Sprint’s old Nextel push-to-talk network.”

clm-8183064b4ed24090c318.text: Thompson argues low-band 800-megahertz spectrum fills coverage gaps between rooftop dish access points where SpaceX cannot mount antennas on every building.

evidence.locator: § Distributed Cellular: “still, it can’t have access points on every building, so this spectrum purchase fills in the gaps in letting those sites reach more places.”

clm-63d732acc11f78c2c531.text: SpaceX announced Starlink Mobile will combine its 2-gigahertz mid-band satellite constellation in space with low-band terrestrial spectrum to ensure indoor and outdoor cellular coverage.

evidence.locator: § Distributed Cellular: “Starlink Mobile will deploy a flexible architecture combining our satellite-to-mobile constellation in space with an advanced terrestrial deployment that can seamlessly connect devices everywhere.”

clm-fa1bece621727eb9f35f.text: SpaceX noted that most existing mobile handsets already support the underused 800-megahertz low-band spectrum without needing hardware alterations.

evidence.locator: § Distributed Cellular: “Critically, most existing mobile devices already support this underused band.”

clm-825d5c168203a681095b.text: Thompson argues SpaceX applies its low-orbit satellite swarm strategy to mobile networks by deploying large numbers of lower-capacity ground access points linked by software and space backhaul.

evidence.locator: § Distributed Cellular: “the company’s approach to mobile is in the same vein, leveraging its satellite advantage to build out massively more ground access points with relatively lower capacity”

clm-6fb25c8c33e2036deb83.text: Thompson notes that unlike in-flight satellite broadband where airlines select providers, consumer mobile wireless requires SpaceX to win over individual retail customers from entrenched carriers.

evidence.locator: § Distributed Cellular: “when it comes to consumer cellular services, the decision makers are not airline executives but individual customers.”
